Justice for Jayde

By: Bernadette Maguire | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
An alleged love triangle, a beautiful young teacher abducted and murdered and the social media storm that followed.

Summary:
We piece together the intriguing and tragic trail of events that led to the murder of Jayde Panayiotou. Why was she murdered? Was her husband Christopher having an affair with one of his employees 26 year old Chantelle Coutts? Had he taken out life insurance on her life?

On Monday Christopher Panayiotou was charged with conspiracy to murder, murder, kidnapping and robbery with aggravated circumstances.
A bouncer from his club in PE was also arrested and charged and now a third arrest has been made.

Why has this story captivated the imaginations of so many South Africans? Why has her murder hit the headlines, when 45others murdered on the same day haven't... and how has social media been harnessed to raise awareness?

We will try to find a second case study - someone else who was murdered on the same day in the same province and ask why their murder hasn't been high profile?

How does the flow of information on social media raise the profile of a case? How does it influence and galvanise police work? And even raise the bar in terms of court appearances simply because people rally behind the victims?

We will also try and get exclusives with family, teachers, access to her classroom and try to verify as many facts as possible,in a bid to piece together the various pieces of the puzzle.

Press Release:


Justice for Jayde
An alleged love triangle, a young teacher abducted and murdered. Her story has captivated the imagination of many South Africans who first learnt of her disappearance on social media. Carte Blanche follows intriguing events that led to the tragic murder of Jayde Panayiotou and to the arrest of the alleged mastermind behind the crime – her husband – and his accomplices.


Script:


Justice for Jayde

VO: 16”
This image of Jayde Panayoitou went viral after her sister Toni Inggs sent out a desperate plea for help when she was abducted nearly 3 weeks ago. She was found murdered a day later, creating an outcry.

Link
About 47 people are murdered in SA every day, so why did Jayde’s murder dominate headlines and create such outrage around the country – perhaps the answer lies in the massive social media campaign that was launched after her abduction.

VO:
Social media expert Sarah Britten says the immediacy of information fuelled the interest.

Sarah:
People cared about Jayde in particular because there was a story in it, there was initially a crisis, this woman had disappeared, we need to find her, what if, what it what if…so that created a sense of anticipation, whereas the other murders that were reported that day were reported after the fact.

VO:
Marilyn Woods the headmistress at the school Jayde taught at says she’s never seen such a huge response.

Marilyn
I think Jayde’s sister did a fantastic job in getting it out there I mean Toni was desperate, she did everything to get it out there and I mean that got people on board. Locally, the radio station, all the town and all the people.

Link:
At six thirty in the morning, on the 21st of April Jayde was standing here outside her complex in Port Elizabeth, waiting for a colleague to give her a lift to school, when her colleague arrived, she wasn’t here, and fears began to grow that she had been abducted. Shortly thereafter she was reported missing.


VO: 10”
Her friend and colleague Karen Potgieter couldn’t understand why anyone would want to hurt her kind, gentle and fun loving friend.

Karen:
She was so…she loved people and she loved animals. Everything about her was about dedication. You know she was always involved. You know this red lipstick campaign for abuse against women and children, she’d get us all involved. And then she was out in Malabar, you know one of the township areas handing out food and blankets and feeding animals on the side of the road.

VO: 14”
Reports soon surfaced that money had been withdrawn from Jayde’s account at an ATM in Kwanobuhle. So local farmer Charles Ranger paid helicopter pilot, John Huddleston to fine comb the area.

John:
We flew around the areas around the prison area and around Greenbushes, we followed roads that he thought they could have taken had they planned the kidnapping before the time.

VO: 15”
Police are said to have kept the search going through most of the night – and as the hours ticked by fear started mounting.

Marilyn:
In my heart you always have that fear once someone has been abducted and been away for so long.


VO: 5”
Local journalist Cara Lee Scheun followed the police helicopter to the scene.

Cara Lee:
It just hovered in the once place outside Uitenhage. Then the police rushed and everyone rushed after.


John link:
Then people’s worst fears were realized. Jayde’s body was found on a farm near Kwanobuhle, a township adjacent to Uitenhage.

Twitter posts jayde….blue lights/school VO: 7”
Almost instantly news of her death surfaced on social media. The police arrived at the school.

Marilyn:
I just burst out crying what else, I was distraught. I was glad in a way that I had that moment with the police. With strangers. Because then I just let loose. It was no problem. Because I felt from the start, that I can’t do this in from of my staff, can’t do that in front of my staff…they need me.

John:
So it fell to you to break the news?

Marilyn:
Yes. It was the only time since Jayde’s missing and subsequent death that there was an outpouring of crying. And I let them do it and I let them get it out and the teachers moved around the hall and let them do it and get it out.

VO:4”
The residents reacted with a mixture of outrage and sympathy.

Could lose Marilyn:
That evening I had people phoning me and saying there were hundreds of people at the school. I didn’t organize it – it was spontaneous. I didn’t even know about it. They filled the walls next to the gate with flowers and they lit hundreds of candles.

VO: 18”
Police released a photo, from the ATM camera of one of allegedsuspects withdrawing money from Jayde’s account. The murder galvanized residents of the metro to vent their anger. More than 4000 people joined to share their outrage over crime levels in marches and rallies across the metro.
Social media also provided a platform for people to grieve

Sarah:
Jayde was unusual. She was a teacher, you liked her, she was middle class…things like this are not supposed to happen to nice middle class people waiting for lifts at six thirty in the morning.

VO: 21
The Catholic Church in Newton park was overflowing on the day of her funeral. Jayde’s husband, Christopher Panayoutiou delivered a touching eulogy. But just days later, Christopher was arrested along with Luthando Siyoli, a bouncer who worked at his nightclub in the suburb of Algoa Park. The eulogy it emerged had been plagiarized from the internet.

John link:
Uitenhage is a small town where people’s lives often intersect, many people here knew Jayde and Chris and the two families so there’s a real sense of shock that something as tragic and as terrible as this could ever have happened.

VO: 12
Both Jayde and Christopher had grown up in the town, they were high school sweethearts, they’d attended brother and sister schools. Christopher was known as a gentle and kind person.

Cara Lee:
They can’t believe it. They wont believe it. They refuse. They will chase you if you say something, if you ask something and they have.

John link
It’s reported that Christopher Panayiotou was nabbed in a police sting operation. According to those reports one of his employees bouncer Luthando Siyoli was instructed to call Chris to a meeting where he was to demand more money – apparently because of the media hype surrounding the case.

VO: 13”
Media reports suggest that he may have paid R30 000 for the alleged hit. Linking Christopher to the alleged hit men is critical says law faculty lecturer at the local university, Desiree David. She hopes they learnt from the Dewani case.

Desiree:
With the Dewani case I think we can say it wasn;t a failure of justice so much as it was the investigation being incomplete or not up to the required standard. So in the absence of sufficient evidence to establish a prima facie case against the against the accused irrespective of what we as the public know about the matter, the presiding officer can only make a decision within the parameters of the evidence that has been presented.

VO: 32”
On Monday this week Jayde’s husband, Christopher appeared in the PE magistrates court on charges of murder, conspiracy to commit murder, kidnapping and robbery with aggravated circumstances. On Tuesday, the suspected triggerman Sizwe Vumazonke also appeared in the dock with a heavily swollen face.

It’s also been revealed that he is out on bail for his alleged role in a violent armed robbery in December last year. Bouncer Luthando Siyoli also appeared in court on Thursday. All 3 men will appear in court again on the 19th of June – but that’s likely to be a mere postponement.

Desiree:
The investigation has to be given an opportunity to run its course. We don’t want a rush to justice and a rush to get into a court room and have a situation where the evidence that is presented is not of a sufficient standard to allow the state to make its case.

VO: 7”
It’s also suspected, given the level of co-operation from Siyoli that he may turn state witness.

Desiree:
It may well happen that he decides to go that way because what it will mean for him is that it will offer him immunity and that would be dependent on his giving testimony that is truthful, that is correct and that he does not try to gloss over things.

Create google map VO: 36
Information is sketchy but it appears Jayde was abducted outside her house at around 6:30am and driven straight through to a farm adjacent to Kwanobuhle. Farmworkers report having heard shots at around 7am.
The motive for the murder that has rocked the metro still seems unclear. Media reports claimed that Christopher was having a secret affair with this woman Chanelle Coutts who rose up the ranks in his grocery store from cashier to manager in a matter of months.

VO: 6”
We visited his store and his nightclub but found both staff and locals unwilling to comment.

Upsound
I can’t tell you that sorry…


VO: 10”
Whatever the motive it won’t bring back the teacher affectionately known as Mrs P. But her friends and colleagues want to keep the beautiful memories of her alive.

Karen:
It’s because of that open loving nature that she touches something in everyone.

Marilyn:
Whever I used to walk past her I used to say Jaydee, and she used to smile. She was such a petite little person, neat, modern in the way she used to dress.. She took great pride.


VO: 4
Even from the photos her love of life shines through.

John: I hear that came to the fore at a hockey tournament recently.

Karen:
There was a jumping castle. And we decided no-ones watching lets just have a fun moment. And we had a ball and that is typically who Jayde is.

VO: 6”
Last week the school paid a poignant goodbye to Jayde on the hockey field.

Marilyn:
They wrote messages to Jayde on the balloons, we love you and we miss you and all sorts of things. And then the whole school gathered on the top hockey field and then we just let the balloons go and as the balloons went up into the air we shouted we love you Mrs Panayoitou and we sang the school song.

Karen:
It’s just so Jayde so I think that the way we’ve gone about celebrating her and you know that’s important that we celebrate her and not just hang our heads and mourn.


Promos:

Promo 1 – 10 seconds

VO: 10”
The murder of a beautiful young Eastern Cape teacher, the outrage that follows and then the shock when her husband and his alleged accomplices are arrested.


Promo 2:

VO: 4
Jayde Panayoitou’s abduction and murder sparked an outcry on social media.

Sarah:
…after the fact

VO; 3”
And it galvanized the Port Elizabeth community to vent.


Promo 3:

VO: 5”
Slain teacher Jayde Panayiotou;s gentle fun loving spirit shines through in her photos.

Karen:
Touched something in all of us.

VO: 4.5
We unpack the events that led to the arrest of her husband Christopher.

Why has her murder hit the headlines, when 45others murdered on the same day haven't... and how has social media been harnessed to raise awareness? We will try to find a second case study - someone else who was murdered on the same day in the same province and ask why their murder hasn't been high profile? How does the flow of information on social media raise the profile of a case? How does it influence and galvanise police work? And even raise the bar in terms of court appearances simply because people rally behind the victims? We will also try and get exclusives with family, teachers, access to her classroom and try to verify as many facts as possible,in a bid to piece together the various pieces of the puzzle.
